title: How AI is changing Software Engineering: A Conversation with Gergely Orosz, @pragmaticengineer
summary: Gergely Orosz at AI Engineer: token-maxing incentives, individual vs team gains, the widening engineer role, big-tech internal AI infra.

assertions.quote: people are just running autonomous agents to build junk honestly for the sake of having that number go up

verdicts.note: Goodhart's law applies: Orosz reports leaderboards and spend targets at large firms prompting busywork; consistent with past experience of line-of-code metrics.

assertions.quote: individually it's it certainly is and as teams we're kind of like a bit question mark

verdicts.note: DORA 2024/25 and Faros 2025 found individual output up while organizational delivery metrics stayed flat or worsened; review and integration become the bottleneck.

assertions.quote: they felt 20% more productive, but ... they were 20% less productive

verdicts.note: Accurately reports METR's July 2025 RCT (16 devs, ~19% slower); the finding is specific to that setting and early-2025 tools.
METR RCT: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks in their own mature repos; allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%.

assertions.quote: it just takes a long time to get good at it and you need to keep doing it

verdicts.note: Learning curves are real (METR's one dev with >50h Cursor experience was faster), but evidence that ramp-up reliably flips results is thin.

There was no improvement across the first 50 hours of Cursor use, and dropping early tasks didn't change the slowdown. One developer with more than 50 hours did speed up, so a high skill ceiling is plausible but underpowered.

assertions.quote: the tester role has collapsed into software engineer ... devops collapse into here ... now we're starting to have the product role

verdicts.note: The trend toward 'product engineers' and DevOps ownership predates AI; AI plausibly speeds it, but evidence is anecdotal.

assertions.quote: their two pizza teams are now just one pizza teams

verdicts.note: Some companies report smaller teams and AI-native startups run lean, but industry-wide team-size data are thin and confounded by cost cutting.

assertions.quote: if you actually enable your non-coding ... collaborators to code actually they are more productive

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.
45% of sources stress accessibility for novices and non-programmers. That evidence is mostly grey literature and centered on prototypes.
